title: Cod Meuniere
subtitle: Pan-fried cod in brown butter with lemon
excerpt: Meuniere is a French technique where fish is dusted in flour and pan-fried in butter until golden, then finished with a squeeze of lemon and more butter foamed in the pan. Cod works beautifully here with its firm, flaky flesh. The whole dish is on the table in 20 minutes.
sourceNotes: Meuniere is a classic French preparation traditionally used for sole. The name refers to the miller's wife, a nod to the flour coating. Cod is a straightforward substitute that is easier to source.

content.text: Pat the cod very dry with kitchen paper before dusting in flour. Wet fish steams rather than fries and you will not get the golden crust. Brown butter moves from golden to burned in seconds, so have the lemon and parsley ready before it goes in.

items.prepNote: 4 pieces, skin on if possible, patted dry

content.text: Season the cod fillets on both sides with salt and pepper. Dust the flesh side in flour and shake off any excess.

Heat the oil and 30g of the butter in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. When the butter is foaming, lay the cod flesh-side down. Cook without moving for 4 to 5 minutes until golden and the flesh is opaque halfway up the side.
Flip gently and cook on the skin side for 2 to 3 minutes until just cooked through. Transfer to warm plates.
Wipe the pan clean with kitchen paper. Return to the heat and add the remaining 70g of butter. Cook, swirling the pan, until the butter turns a deep golden colour and smells nutty.
Remove from the heat, squeeze in the lemon juice and add the parsley. The butter will bubble up. Pour immediately over the fish and serve with lemon wedges.

items.cause: Pan not hot enough or fish moved too early.
items.fix: Wait until it lifts cleanly, then turn it.

items.cause: Heat too high or left unattended.
items.fix: Discard and start with fresh butter over lower heat.
Dry the fish thoroughly with kitchen paper next time.
